subject: Transportation Systems
title: Peak vs. Off-Peak Ridership
description: A micro-lesson that makes Peak vs. Off-Peak Ridership usable.

hook.text: Morning and evening rush hours can account for 60% of total daily ridership. The rest of the day is quiet.

buildup.text: Agencies buy enough buses and trains to handle the peak. Most of that fleet sits idle at midday.

discovery.text: The cost of peak service is enormous—drivers, vehicles, and maintenance all scale to the busiest hour.

twist.text: Remote work flattened peaks. But agencies can't easily cut peak service without angering commuters.

climax.text: Off-peak pricing and events encourage travel outside rush hours to spread demand more evenly.

punchline.text: Transit's biggest expense is the two hours everyone travels at once.

quiz.question: Why is peak service so expensive for transit agencies?
options: Higher fuel prices in the morning
Extra vehicles, drivers, and maintenance for the busiest hours
